chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who died and left a young child who was being breastfed, saying: 'The wage of the child's breastfeeding is taken from what he inherits from his father and mother.'
ai.seo_question: Who pays for the breastfeeding of an orphaned infant according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle that the maintenance cost of a nursing infant is a charge against the child's own inheritance from both parents, ensuring the financial burden does not fall exclusively on the mother or the general estate. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view of breastfeeding as a right of the child funded by their assets, reflecting the equitable distribution of posthumous financial responsibilities. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the interplay between inheritance law (*fara'id*) and child maintenance (*nafaqah*) in early Islamic legal practice.
